title: Build map furniture for a ggplot2 map — make_map_furniture
text: xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax Numeric. Map extent WGS84 decimal degrees. xmin must less xmax; boxes crossing antimeridian supported. crs Target projection, anything sf::st_transform() accepts: EPSG code PROJ string. projected, metres unit, projection use mapr() ggplot2::coord_sf(). buffer Numeric. Margin around frame sides, metres. white space graticule labels written , needs wide enough hold . Defaults 500000 (500 km), suits ocean basin; North Sea map around 200000 works well. lat_by, lon_by Numeric. Spacing graticules labels degrees. Positions snap multiples values falling inside extent, lat_by = 5 50 62 degree extent gives 50, 55 60. densify Numeric. Maximum segment length degrees used densifying bounding box, passed sf::st_segmentize(). Smaller values give smoother curved edges cost vertices.

title: Build map furniture for a ggplot2 map — make_map_furniture
text: named list components: flyway_wgs84 sfc polygon densified frame EPSG:4326. flyway polygon transformed crs. Draw fill = NA border around map. cookie sfc polygon covering buffered frame map extent punched . Draw filled white, data layers labels. parallels sf points along western edge, columns lat, lon label. Pass lat ggplot2::scale_y_continuous() breaks draw matching graticules. meridians sf points along southern edge, columns lat, lon label. Pass lon ggplot2::scale_x_continuous() breaks draw matching graticules. xlim, ylim Length-2 numeric vectors CRS units, ggplot2::coord_sf().

title: Build map furniture for a ggplot2 map — make_map_furniture
text: cookie-cutter mask, rectangle map extent punched . Drawn white top data layers, hides anything spilling past edge map leaves clean margin. graticule positions labels along western southern edges, already formatted "55\u00b0N", "5\u00b0W" . plot limits projected units, ready pass straight ggplot2::coord_sf(). bounding box densified geographic coordinates projection, edges map follow curved graticules rather straight lines target projection. Use alongside mapr(), supplies land. land needs reach past frame every side, since cookie hides anything beyond . See vignette("mapr") step--step guide building map.

title: Build map furniture for a ggplot2 map — make_map_furniture
code: prj <- "+proj=utm +zone=30 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"  mf <- make_map_furniture(   xmin = -7.5, xmax = 10, ymin = 50, ymax = 62,   crs = prj,   buffer = 200000,   lat_by = 5,   lon_by = 5 )  # Plot limits, in metres, because the projection is in metres mf$xlim #> [1]  -22444.32 1630226.78  # The graticule labels mf$parallels$label #> [1] "50°N" "55°N" "60°N" mf$meridians$label #> [1] "5°W"  "0°"   "5°E"  "10°E"  # \donttest{ library(sf) #> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE library(ggplot2)  data(gannets) gannets_sf <- st_as_sf(gannets, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) land <- mapr(gannets, prj, buff = 400000) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_intersection assumes that they #> are planar  # Layer order matters: land and data, then the cookie, then the frame, # then the labels ggplot() +   theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +   geom_sf(data = land, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2) +   geom_sf(data = gannets_sf, aes(colour = id), size = 0.1,           show.legend = FALSE) +   geom_sf(data = mf$cookie, fill = "white", colour = NA) +   geom_sf(data = mf$flyway, fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = mf$meridians$lon) +   scale_y_continuous(breaks = mf$parallels$lat) +   coord_sf(xlim = mf$xlim, ylim = mf$ylim, crs = prj, expand = FALSE) +   theme(axis.text = element_blank(),         axis.title = element_blank()) +   geom_sf_text(data = mf$parallels, aes(label = label),                size = 2.5, colour = "grey40",                nudge_x = -15000, hjust = 1) +   geom_sf_text(data = mf$meridians, aes(label = label),                size = 2.5, colour = "grey40",                nudge_y = -15000, vjust = 1)  # }

title: mapr 0.2.0
text: mapr() now takes coastline rnaturalearth rather rworldmap. default scale = "medium" detailed old rworldmap coastline; use scale = "small" something closer previous output. mapr() now projects sf input prj one supplied. Previously CRS sf object always used, prj silently ignored.

title: mapr 0.2.0
text: mapr() works sf 1.0 later, uses spherical geometry (s2) default. function switches s2 runs restores setting afterwards. Invalid coastline polygons now repaired sf::st_make_valid() rather st_buffer(x, 0), longer works repair s2. mapr() gives clearer errors missing projection, data without CRS, data frames without lon lat columns.
